resumen: Stepping up onto a box with one leg and coming down under control. The top foot never moves: what rises is the whole body.
ejecucion: Stand facing a box about 35 cm high, a dumbbell in each hand.
Place one whole foot on top, heel well inside the box.
Push up with that leg, without pushing off with the bottom one.
At the top the hip is extended and the bottom leg is just along for the ride.
Lower slowly until your toe touches the floor and repeat before switching.
matices: The catch is the launch: if you push off with the bottom foot, the leg that was meant to work barely does anything. In the cited study, the lateral step-up produced less gluteus medius activation than the single-leg squat, though more than standing: a useful intermediate step.
